title: How do we divide large numbers and name the answers?
description: Three large divisions are made small by removing the same zeros from both numbers. Each answer is then read in the Indian and the American systems. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking the first answer is nine hundred thirty.
teaching_notes: One idea: remove the same number of zeros from both numbers, divide, and then name the answer in each system. Ask the class to count the zeros at the end of each number before any dividing is done. Watch for students who remove the zeros and then drop a zero again from the answer.

source: 13,95,000 ÷ 150, 10,50,00,000 ÷ 700, 52,00,00,00,000 ÷ 130: Calculate the quotient and read the number in both Indian and American naming systems.
video_script.why: The child has multiplied large numbers by setting zeros aside, and now divides large numbers the same way and names the answers in both systems.
video_script.substitution: Remove the same number of zeros from both numbers, divide the digits that are left, and read the answer in the Indian and American systems.
video_script.anchor: Three divisions written in a column: 13,95,000 ÷ 150, 10,50,00,000 ÷ 700 and 52,00,00,00,000 ÷ 130, with a box for the Indian name and a box for the American name beside each.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko removes one zero from both numbers to get 1,39,500 ÷ 15, and then drops another zero from the answer 9,300 to write 930. But 930 × 150 = 1,39,500, only a tenth of 13,95,000.
video_script.payoff_line: Equal zeros removed from both numbers leave the answer unchanged

final_answer.spoken: nine thousand three hundred, one lakh fifty thousand, and forty crore

never_show: the first quotient as one number before the answer beat
maths_rules: 13,95,000 ÷ 150 = 1,39,500 ÷ 15 (one zero removed from both); 15 × 9000 = 1,35,000 and 15 × 300 = 4,500, so 9000 + 300 = 9,300; named the same in both systems: nine thousand three hundred
check: 930 × 150 = 1,39,500, which is one tenth of 13,95,000
video_script.design: One idea: remove equal zeros from both numbers, divide, then name. Wrong idea: Keeko says nine hundred thirty. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three large numbers are divided by numbers that end in zeros.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We must find each answer, and read it in the Indian and the American systems.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Which zeros can be set aside?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The same number of zeros can be removed from both numbers before we divide.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Indian names use lakh and crore, while American names use thousand, million and billion.

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, three divisions.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Thirteen lakh ninety five thousand divided by one hundred fifty.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Ten crore fifty lakh divided by seven hundred.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Five thousand two hundred crore divided by one hundred thirty.

beats.on_screen: To find: each answer, and its Indian name and American name

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find each answer, and name it in both systems.

marks.m1: one zero slides off 13,95,000 and one zero slides off 150
marks.m2: 15 × 9000 = 1,35,000 is written, and 4,500 is left over
marks.m3: 15 × 300 = 4,500 is written and the parts 9000 and 300 are lit

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, remove one zero from each number of the first division.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Fifteen times nine thousand is one lakh thirty five thousand. Four thousand five hundred is left over.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Fifteen times three hundred is four thousand five hundred, so the parts are nine thousand and three hundred.

marks.m1: two zeros slide off 10,50,00,000 and two zeros slide off 700
marks.m3: 105 ÷ 7 = 15 is written, and 4 small zeros are placed after 15

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, remove two zeros from each number of the second division.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ten lakh fifty thousand is one hundred five times ten thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>One hundred five divided by seven is fifteen, and four zeros go back at the end.

marks.m1: one zero slides off 52,00,00,00,000 and one zero slides off 130

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, remove one zero from each number of the third division.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five hundred twenty crore is fifty two times ten crore.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Fifty two divided by thirteen is four, so we get four times ten crore.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 9,300; 1,50,000 = 1 lakh 50 thousand = 150 thousand; 40,00,00,000 = 40 crore = 400 million

marks.m1: the first answer is written and boxed
marks.m2: the second answer is written with its two names and boxed
marks.m3: the third answer is written with its two names and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Equal zeros removed from both numbers leave the answer unchanged. The first answer is nine thousand three hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The second is one lakh fifty thousand, or one hundred fifty thousand.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The third is forty crore, or four hundred million.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the divisions
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 930 crossed out; 930 × 150 = 1,39,500, only a tenth of 13,95,000

marks.m3: 1,39,500 is placed beside 13,95,000 with a tenth marked between them

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the first answer is nine hundred thirty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Let us multiply back. Nine hundred thirty times one hundred fifty is one lakh thirty nine thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is only a tenth of the number in the question. The answer must be ten times bigger.
